newsitem.title: UK: UK CBI sets out post-election priorities.
newsitem.headline: UK CBI sets out post-election priorities.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said the main concern of the next British government should be to ensure macro-economic stability.

"Our paramount concern is that we have stability of the key features of economic policy, with tight control of public finances and low and stable inflation," CBI director-general Adair Turner said in a statement.
"That is the vital context within which other choices should be made."

He said the five policy areas the CBI intended to concentrate on in 1997 were economic and monetary union, labour market flexibility, education and training, manufacturing and transport infrastructure.
Turner said these were policies that demanded attention if Britain was to succeed and prosper in the global economy.
